newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks lose ground despite OTE strength.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks lose ground despite OTE strength.

text.p: Greek shares tracked the performance of major international bourses on Monday on the back of Wall Street's weak show on Friday, but strength in OTE telecom helped limit overall losses.
"Trading volume remains meagre amidst the peak of the summer holiday season and prices sway easily under the influence of external factors," said Athanasios Trikatzis, broker at Hermes Brokerage.

News of a 3.11 percent fall in Wall Street stocks on Friday, the combined result of concerns for a falling dollar and corporate profits, was closely monitored by local market players and was cited as a reason for Monday's drift in the Athens bourse's benchmark index.
Nervousness in foreign equity markets took its toll on Greek stocks which remain directionless within a narrow trading range around 1,600 points, Trikatzis said.

"I think investors used the conditions in international markets as an excuse to take profits on a quiet 100-point rise of the benchmark index in recent days on practically no fresh news," said a fund manager who wished to keep his anonymity.
The market remains vibrant and investor interest in equities is rather high, the fund manager added.

The unrest in international capital markets overshadowed a 30 basis point cut in the Bank of Greece's basic deposit facility rate to 11.30 percent, effective Monday, while leaving the floor rate unchanged at 9.60 percent.
"The major issue at this point remains the government's large fiscal needs for the coming month, affecting the course of interest rates," said Hermes Brokerage's Trikatzis.
Fiscal needs for September are estimated at 2.1 trillion drachmas.
The finance ministry announced a 10 basis point cut in its 12-month T-bills to be offered to the public on August 20, followed by an auction of 100 billion drachmas of FRNs on August 21.
The Athens benchmark index lost 1.39 percent or 22.91 points at 1,622.90 from Thursday's 1,638.47 close.
All sector sub-indices settled lower. Industrials led the market with a 2.03 percent drop, with banks softening 1.54 percent.
Turnover reached 7.8 billion drachmas on volume of 1.8 million shares, including a block of 30,000 shares of Alpha Credit Bank traded at 20,000 drachmas.
Decliners beat advancers 149 to 46 with 14 shares unchanged on 209 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $11.0-$11.4. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,132-1,162 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,118-1,178 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock climbed 60 drachmas to 6,610.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 692.58-736.79 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $76.49-$79.33. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,815-4,044 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $12.11 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 229-261 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
